content:
Is it possible to define or model inductive types in Veil? For example, if I wanted to define a simple arithmetic expression language I might define it in Lean as something like:

inductive Expr where
| Num : nat -> Expr
| Add : Expr -> Expr -> Expr
| Mul : Expr -> Expr -> Expr
| Sub : Expr -> Expr -> Expr
| Div : Expr -> Expr -> Expr

How would you normally model something like this type in Veil? The veil_decl macro for veil 2.0 currently displays an error message that "proxy equivalence: recursive inductive types are not supported (and are usually infinite)"

The issue you're seeing comes from how veil_decl tries to automatically derive certain instances (e.g., Hashable, Ord) for tagged data types. In particular, deriving Std.TransOrd and Std.LawfulEqOrd relies on the proxy_equiv% elaborator from Mathlib, which does not seem to support recursive inductive types. This is what leads to the error message you encountered.

In the latest veil-2.0-preview, these derivation failures should result in warnings rather than errors. In principle, you could also provide Std.TransOrd and Std.LawfulEqOrd instances for your Expr type manually.

That said, these instances are not always required in practice. Could you share a bit more about how you intend to use Expr in Veil? That would help us better understand your use case.

Ah ok, I should be able to provide those manually then. Really I want to model a Dolev-Yao style adversary using derivations (the equivalent of recipes in Tamarin). So I want to have an inductive definition of a derivation that looks something like:

inductive Derivation where
| Encrypt : (plaintext: Derivation) -> (key: Derivation) -> Derivation
| Decrypt : (ciphertext: Derivation) -> (key: Derivation) -> Derivation
| Pair : Derivation -> Derivation -> Derivation
| Left : (pair: Derivation) -> Derivation
| Right : (pair: Derivation) -> Derivation
...

and then define a partial derivation function on terms that looks something like:

def derive(d: Derivation, k: Knowledge) : Option Term =
  match d with
  | Encrypt d_plaintext d_key =>
    match derive(d_plaintext, k), derive(d_key, k) with
    | Some p, Some (Key key) => Some (senc p key)
    ...
  ...

I then want to reason about what an adversary can or cannot derive from their knowledge. It should be straightforward to encode the derive function into a veil relation with an invariant that derive is a function (derive(d, k) = t1 /\ derive(d, k) = t2 -> t1 = t2). It seems like the only extra thing I need to do, to encode these derivations into Veil, is just provide the TransOrd and LawfulEqOrd instances manually for the Derivation type. Are there any other issues you see (off the top of your head) with encoding derivations into veil in this manner?

I see, thanks for the detailed explanation. This helps clarify your setup.

One thing to note is that Std.TransOrd and Std.LawfulEqOrd are typically only needed when executing Veil actions (e.g., for model checking). So if you don't actually need to execute actions, you may not need to provide these instances at all.

That said, #gen_spec currently tries to generate executable versions of actions by default. So even if execution is not your goal, you might still run into errors. These are not necessarily caused by missing instances; another potential issue is that your relations may involve domains like Derivation, which are infinite. At the moment, Veil's support for execution over such infinite domains is still quite limited (there is only one use case: VeilTest/TestInfDomain.lean), so it's a bit unclear how well this would work in practice.

On the other hand, if you use a concrete inductive type like Derivation directly as part of a relation's domain, my impression is that you would likely need to rely on manual proofs. The current SMT query translation is probably not yet able to handle this kind of structure effectively.

I then want to reason about what an adversary can or cannot derive from their knowledge.

From your description, it sounds like you might mainly be interested in using Veil for verification in this case, is that right?

Yup that's correct! I'm already doing verification for protocols in this setting, but the proofs are a bit tedious to get right and rely on a variant of a bisimulation relation. I have a hunch that I could encode parts of the proofs I'm trying to into veil, which would ideally be able to provide nice counter-examples that could speed up iteration in developing a suitable relation. I do expect to run into some issues with what the SMT solver can prove itself (using the encoding from Veil), but I'd like to see where that limit currently is and if it's currently useful for my purposes.

I ended up needing to axiomatize the constructors for the inductive type just using relations. It looks like lean-smt recently added support for encoding inductive structures as datatypes (https://github.com/ufmg-smite/lean-smt/pull/221) that should at least make it easier for Veil to encode inductive types for the SMT backend.

Is an update to the latest lean-smt version (which would require bumping lean support to Lean version 4.29) something you're currently working on or open to accepting contributions for? My understanding is that such a change would first require reconciling the veil lean-smt fork (https://github.com/verse-lab/lean-smt/tree/v4.27.0-for-veil) with the latest lean-smt updates. Are you aware of other major structural changes that might need to be made to Veil, maybe in how counter-examples are reconstructed, that would also need to be made to accommodate an SMT encoding using datatypes?

@Kirby Linvill

Nice. Support for inductive types is definitely something we're hoping to add. I don't expect it to require major changes, but yes, it will likely require some new code to reconstruct counterexamples as Lean values.

I'm currently writing up my dissertation, so unfortunately haven't had much time for maintenance, but I should have time in June to catch up on all the work I've been postponing and properly release Veil 2.0.

Porting our changes onto upstream shouldn't be too difficult. If you think it would be interesting and have time to look into it, I'd appreciate it. No worries if it's not urgent for you — I'll get to it next month.

@Kirby Linvill I upgraded Veil’s lean-smt fork to Lean v4.29.0 a few days ago and pulled in the upstream changes, including the recent datatype encoding support.

If you haven't already started working on this yourself, I can also try upgrading Veil to Lean v4.29.0 over the next couple of days.

@Qiyuan Zhao I haven't had the chance to work on it myself yet, thanks for getting that started! That would be awesome if you have the time. I'd love to try out how the upgraded lean-smt fork and veil work with encoding inductive types.

Good luck on your dissertation George!
